name: Sapna Sweets, Bakers & Restaurant
why_it_matters: The Akhara Bazaar address that locals point tourists to when they ask where to eat real Kulvi food. Their Kulvi Dham — the rice-and-curry feast traditionally served at Kullu weddings — runs as a thali, and their walnut-and-poppy-seed siddu comes with desi ghee from Anni in Rampur.
insider_tip: The siddu is the dish to come for, not the sweets — order it with the dal accompaniment, not just ghee, and you get the wedding-feast version. Mornings are best; the steamer is fresh from 9am.
signature_address: Near Durga Mata Temple, Akhara Bazaar, Kullu 175101

name: Kebabs N Curries
why_it_matters: Akhara Bazaar's go-to for proper tandoor work — open 11am-11pm, opposite Ram Bhag Park. The 4.3-rating restaurant guru locals trust for kebabs when Sapna's pure-veg won't do, and one of the few central-Kullu addresses with a working charcoal tandoor.
insider_tip: Pair the kebab platter with their fresh-squeezed apple juice — Kullu valley orchards are 15 minutes away and the juice is pressed daily, not bottled.
signature_address: Opposite Ram Bhag Park, Akhara Bazaar, Kullu 175101

name: Hot Spice Cafe
why_it_matters: A short walk from the Dussehra Maidan in Dhalpur — the cafe families pick over Mall Road's noisier dhabas. Hours run 8:30am-9:30pm, so it doubles as both a quick breakfast stop before driving up to Manali and an after-temple dinner.
insider_tip: It's quieter than the Akhara Bazaar end of town — sit upstairs with a plate of momos and you can hear the Beas instead of horns.

name: Miya Je Delight
why_it_matters: A two-dish kitchen on Circuit House Road near OLS School — siddu and momos, that's the menu. The siddu is the local Himachali wheat dumpling done properly: yeast-fermented dough, walnut-poppy stuffing, steamed in front of you. Sells out by 4pm most days.
insider_tip: Arrive before 2pm. Order one siddu with ghee, one with the dal accompaniment — you'll learn why the dish has nothing to do with momos despite people calling them 'big momos'.
signature_address: Circuit House Road, near OLS School, Dhalpur, Kullu 175101

name: The Sarvari (HPTDC) Restaurant
why_it_matters: Himachal Pradesh Tourism Development Corporation's Kullu property at Shastri Nagar, Dhalpur — the dependable government-run kitchen with a bar and lawn seating. Solid for travellers who want a sit-down meal away from the bazaar bustle, and a fallback when Sapna and Kebabs N Curries are full.
insider_tip: It's set slightly above town in Shastri Nagar — quieter than central Dhalpur, with a lawn that works well for kids on the run after a long Manali-direction drive.

name: The Silvermoon (HPTDC) Restaurant
why_it_matters: HPTDC's second Kullu restaurant — central Dhalpur, near the HPTDC Tourist Information Centre, more accessible than the Sarvari uphill. Multi-cuisine kitchen, AC dining, the kind of safe family lunch stop that's reliable rather than exciting.
insider_tip: Easier to walk in than the Sarvari — handier if you're already in central Dhalpur for the Dussehra Ground or the Raghunath Temple climb.

name: Planet Food
why_it_matters: One of the workhorse Dhalpur eating joints — multi-cuisine menu (Indian, Chinese, South Indian, fast food), large enough for groups and corporate tour buses. Picks up the overflow when the HPTDC restaurants are full.
insider_tip: Stick to the Indo-Chinese end of the menu — the South Indian section is functional but not regional. Hakka noodles + paneer chilli is the locals' combo.

name: Punjabi Dhaba
why_it_matters: An Akhara Bazaar fixture for over three decades — a no-frills dhaba near the petrol pump that's been doing Punjabi-Mughlai for the local crowd longer than most Kullu travellers have been visiting. Plates land in five minutes; rotis come straight off the tandoor.
insider_tip: Sit on the bench facing the kitchen, not the road — you'll see the rotis hit the tandoor and your dal getting tempered. Order the lassi in summer, the masala chai in winter.
signature_address: Near Petrol Pump, Akhara Bazaar, Kullu 175101
